name: Nick Carroll
strengths: Carroll triggers downhill from a deep safety look and wraps in space — alley fills and open-field form tackles, not just a hit.
Carroll tracks the deep ball from a high / two-high alignment and finishes with it — eyes and range from the compact 5-10 frame.
Carroll shows the same burst on kickoff coverage: sprint, break down, and finish the tackle on the returner.
weaknesses: Carroll (5-10 / 170) still needs mass before every SEC box collision is a win — fill-out is the next step. Sophomore highlight reel, not All-22 volume.
comparison: Carroll comps to Alohi Gilman — 5-10 compact safety who wins with instincts, downhill trigger, and wrap tackles more than length (size-matched within ~1" of Carroll’s 5-10 / 170 frame; same build family as he fills).
projection: Carroll projects as special-teams and nickel/package early, then compete for a starting safety job — starter ceiling as a compact every-down S once the 170-pound frame fills.
schemeFit: Carroll fits Chris Collins’ safety room as a compact deep-to-box hybrid who can trigger downhill, wrap in space, and grow into nickel and split-safety snaps as the frame fills.
